info.title: Alloy Public API
info.description:
The Alloy Public API. This artifact describes ONLY endpoints that exist. Coverage is enforced in both directions: a documented path with no route, or a route under /api/v1 with no documentation, fails Alloy's build.

Authority is never chosen by the caller. An access token resolves to exactly one installation, and that installation determines the organization, the granted scopes and the resource boundary. There is no org_id parameter anywhere in this contract.

post.summary: Exchange an installation credential for an access token
post.description: Client-credentials grant. The returned token is opaque, expires in 15 minutes, and carries no authority of its own — scopes and resource boundary are re-read from the installation on every request, so a revocation takes effect on the next call.

get.description: Returns the caller's own application, installation, organization, granted scopes and resource boundary. Touches no domain data. This is the correct first call for any integration: it answers which tenant you are and what you may do, before anything depends on the answer.

Returns sites and units within the installation's organization AND its resource boundary. Requires the `locations.read` scope.

Customer and vendor premises (`location_type = address`) are never returned at any scope — they describe private addresses rather than organizational locations.

Filters narrow the already-authorized set and can never widen it: naming a location outside the boundary returns nothing rather than granting it.

Incremental sync: page the collection once with `cursor`, then store the `sync_token` from the last page you durably processed and pass it back as `since_token` next time. A sync token identifies an exact row, so two records sharing a timestamp cannot be skipped or repeated and there is nothing to rewind. Use `updated_since` only for deliberate time-based reconciliation against a moment you chose.

get.description:
Append-only attendance facts for children at sites within this installation's location boundary.

Nothing in this collection is ever removed or rewritten. A mistake is corrected by a later fact whose `entry_type` is `correction` (it restates) or `reversal` (it voids), and which names the fact it supersedes in `corrects_event_id`. Fold them the way Alloy does: a superseded fact is no longer effective, and a reversal leaves nothing behind but its own record. Because nothing disappears, a consumer that has read every page holds the complete history.

Order and synchronization both advance on `recorded_at` — when Alloy recorded the fact — not on `event_at`. A correction to last week is recorded today and therefore arrives today; ordering by when things happened would file it behind a checkpoint you had already passed.

## Keeping a copy in step

1. Bootstrap: request without `since_token` or `updated_since`.
2. Follow `next_cursor` until it is null, storing each page as you go.
3. When the pass completes, persist the `sync_token` from the last page you consumed. Persist it only after the whole pass succeeded — a token saved mid-pass would skip whatever you did not store.
4. Next time, request with `since_token` set to the value you persisted.
5. Follow `next_cursor` to exhaustion again, then persist the new `sync_token`.

A `sync_token` identifies one record, not an instant, so records sharing a timestamp are neither skipped nor repeated. If you checkpoint with `updated_since` instead, supply the exact `recorded_at` you stopped at — it is matched at full precision.

### Example

Bootstrap, then resume:

```
GET /api/v1/attendance-events?limit=200
  -> { "data": [...], "next_cursor": "eyJ...", "sync_token": "eyJ..." }
GET /api/v1/attendance-events?limit=200&cursor=eyJ...
  -> { "data": [...], "next_cursor": null, "sync_token": "eyJhZ..." }

# store "eyJhZ...", then later:
GET /api/v1/attendance-events?limit=200&since_token=eyJhZ...
  -> only facts recorded after the one that token names
```

Narrow a sync to one site or one child with `site_id` or `child_id`; filters never widen what your installation may read.

post.description:
Record attendance facts for children at locations within this installation's boundary.

Attendance is a ledger, not a mutable record. There is no update and no delete: a mistake is fixed by submitting a **correction**, which restates the fact and names the event it supersedes, or a **reversal**, which voids it and asserts nothing in its place. Both appear through `GET /api/v1/attendance-events` as new facts carrying `corrects_event_id`.

## Each event is judged on its own

This operation is **not atomic**. Every event you send gets its own durable outcome, and one unmapped identifier does not discard the events either side of it. The response is `200` whenever the batch was processed — including when every event was refused — so read `results`, not the status code. Results may be returned in any order; match them by `external_event_id`.

Events are applied in the order you send them, so a correction may name an original earlier in the same batch.

## Retrying is safe

`external_event_id` is the replay identity. If a request times out or you are unsure whether it arrived, send it again: an event Alloy already accepted comes back as `replayed` with the fact it recorded the first time, and nothing is created twice. Reusing an id for DIFFERENT content is a `conflict` — use a new id for a new fact, or submit a correction. You do not need an idempotency header; your own event id is the key.

## Identifiers

Children and rooms are named with YOUR identifiers, as mapped for this installation. Alloy never creates a record from an identifier it does not recognise: an unmapped identifier returns `pending_mapping`, and the event applies when you submit it again after the mapping exists.

## Reading your own writes

An accepted fact is immediately readable through `GET /api/v1/attendance-events` at its `recorded_at` position, so a synchronizing consumer picks it up on the next incremental pass.

200.description: The batch was processed. Every event carries its own outcome.

get.description:
Children participating in service at locations within your boundary. Requires the `children.read` scope.

**Enrollment is what makes a child visible.** A child appears here only when an enrollment agreement places them at a site you can reach. An enrollment that never represented service never makes a child visible: one CANCELED BEFORE IT BEGAN, and one VOIDED as recorded in error. Every other status does make a child visible, including `ended`, so your attendance and billing history stays resolvable. Belonging to the organization is not enough, and this holds even for organization-wide installations — being organization-wide widens which SITES you reach, not what counts as participation in service. If you expect a child and do not see one, check their enrollment first.

**What this resource is not.** It carries identity and lifecycle only. Health, allergy, medical and safeguarding information is never returned by any endpoint in this API. Guardians and contact details are a separate resource with a separate scope: see `GET /api/v1/relationships`.

**Lifecycle.** Poll `status`. A child leaving service becomes `inactive`. Visibility itself can end — a `pending_start` enrollment that is canceled, or an enrollment voided as never-valid — and it is never silent: the enrollment remains readable, turns `canceled`, and its `updated_at` advances, so `GET /api/v1/enrollments?updated_since=...` delivers the change on a normal sync pass. Read `/enrollments` when a child stops appearing here; do not treat it as data loss. A child with commitments at two sites stays visible while any one is uncanceled.

**Your own identifiers.** If you have mapped a child to your own system, `external_id` returns YOUR mapping and only yours. You may also filter by it. Another installation's identifier for the same child is never visible to you.

get.description:
The households of children you can already see. Requires the `households.read` scope.

**A household is an anchor, not an access grant.** It appears because at least one of its children is independently visible to you, and it widens nothing: a sibling enrolled only at a site outside your boundary does not appear in `GET /api/v1/children`, and nothing here reveals that they exist — no member list, no count, no identifier. Households can span sites, so this is a real situation rather than a theoretical one.

To find the children in a household that you may see, call `GET /api/v1/children?household_id=...`. That answer is filtered to your authority, which is the point.

**Not included.** Billing and payment information is never part of this resource.

get.description:
Who a child's adults are, and whether they may collect them. Requires the `relationships.read` scope.

**Relationships are edges, not flags.** Each row is a relationship between one adult and one child, with its own identifier and its own lifecycle. The same person can hold a different relationship to each of their children, which is why this is never flattened into booleans on a child or a person.

A relationship is visible exactly when its child is. This resource never widens the set of people you can see; it describes the people you can already reach.

**`pickup_authorized` is an effective answer, not a stored flag.** Alloy computes it at read time: it is `true` only when collection authority has been granted, nothing currently withdraws it, and the child is within your boundary. It fails closed — if anything is uncertain, it is `false`.

No reason is ever returned and none can be requested. Do not infer one from other fields, and do not treat a `false` as a data error: treat it as the answer. If your workflow needs to know why, that conversation belongs with the operator, not with this API.

**Contact details are a stronger grant.** `email` and `phone` are returned only to installations holding `relationships.contact.read`. Without it the fields are absent from the response entirely, rather than present and empty.

get.description:
Committed enrollment agreements. Requires the `enrollment.read` scope.

Alloy keeps three service commitments separate, and so does this API:

- **Enrollment** — this child is enrolled at this site, from this date. *(here)*
- **Placement** — which room, from when. *(`GET /api/v1/placements`)*
- **Schedule assignment** — which recurring pattern applies. *(`GET /api/v1/schedule-assignments`)*

They change independently, so a child can move rooms without their enrollment changing, and change schedule without moving rooms. Synchronize whichever you actually depend on.

**Lifecycle.** `end_date` is null while the agreement is open. Poll for it to learn that enrollment has ended.

post.description:
Enrolls a child at a site from a date. Requires the `enrollment.write` scope.

**This is a named operation, not a field edit.** The public API has no `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` on any resource. Alloy performs the intent through the same authority its own surfaces use, so its validation and refusals are what you receive.

**Safe to retry.** No idempotency key is needed: Alloy reads the current state before acting, so asking twice converges on one record rather than creating a second. A `200` means it was already in this state; a `201` means it changed.

The site must be inside your boundary, and you must have authority over the child — either the child is already visible to you, or you hold a correlation mapping for them (established with Alloy during onboarding). A mapping lets you enroll a child who is not yet in service, which is the usual case; it does not let you enroll them anywhere you cannot reach. An identifier for something you cannot reach returns `404`, the same as one that does not exist — Alloy will not confirm that a record exists outside your authority.

start_date.description: Optional. Defaults to Alloy's own rules.

200.description: Already in this state — the existing record is returned unchanged.

403.description: The installation does not hold the required scope, or has no authorized location.

409.description: Alloy's domain rules refuse the operation in the record's current state.

get.description:
Committed, effective-dated room placement. Requires the `enrollment.read` scope.

**Corrections arrive as new rows.** When a placement is corrected, Alloy writes a new placement naming the one it replaces in `supersedes_placement_id` rather than editing the original. A copy you already stored is therefore never silently wrong — you will receive the correction through ordinary incremental synchronization.

Rooms and sites are Location identifiers from `GET /api/v1/locations`. There is no second room vocabulary to learn.

get.description:
The committed, effective-dated schedule commitment for a child. Requires the `schedule.read` scope.

**This is the canonical schedule resource.** It is persisted, it is synchronizable, and it tells you what was actually committed: which recurring pattern applies to a child, at which site and room, over which dates.

**Choosing between the two schedule endpoints:**

- Use **this** endpoint when you hold standing intent and need to be told when it changes. It participates fully in incremental synchronization.
- Use **`GET /api/v1/schedule-days`** when you are asking "who is expected on Tuesday". That endpoint derives individual days from these assignments and is a windowed query, not a collection.

Only children appear here. Staff schedules are not part of this resource.

get.summary: Project expected days from committed schedules
get.description:
Answers "who is expected on Tuesday". Requires the `schedule.read` scope.

**These rows are derived, not stored.** Each one is generated from a committed schedule assignment and its recurring pattern. They have no identifier of their own and no change history, which is why this endpoint deliberately returns **no cursor and no sync token**. Do not attempt to synchronize it incrementally — there is nothing to checkpoint against, and any watermark would be one this API could not honour.

If you need change detection, synchronize `GET /api/v1/schedule-assignments` instead and re-project the window yourself. Each returned day names the assignment it came from in `schedule_assignment_id` so you can do exactly that.

**Deterministic.** The same window over the same committed schedules always returns the same days in the same order.

`from` and `to` are required and the window may not exceed 92 days.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day of the window, inclusive.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day of the window, inclusive. At most 92 days after `from`.

parameters.name: child_id
parameters.description: Project only this child's days.

parameters.name: site_id
parameters.description: Project only days at this site.

400.description: The window is missing, inverted or longer than 92 days.

get.description:
People employed at locations within your boundary. Requires the `staff.read` scope.

**Staff is a composition, not a separate record.** Alloy models a staff member as a person plus an employment. This resource presents them together for convenience: `id` is the employment and `person_id` is the human. If someone is employed twice, you will see two rows sharing one `person_id`.

**Visibility follows the assignment, not the organization.** Employment is organization-wide, but a staff member appears here only when their primary location is inside your boundary. Someone with no assigned location is not returned.

**Never included.** Compensation, payroll, tax, HR records, safeguarding and medical information are not part of this API at all. Alloy's own internal access permissions are also never exposed — an application role is not an employment role.

Contact details require the stronger `staff.contact.read` scope.

post.description:
Ends an enrollment. Requires the `enrollment.write` scope.

**This is a named operation, not a field edit.** The public API has no `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` on any resource. Alloy performs the intent through the same authority its own surfaces use, so its validation and refusals are what you receive.

**One intent, three outcomes, chosen by Alloy.** An enrollment that has not started is canceled; one in service is marked ending on the date you give; one whose end date has passed is closed. You do not need to know which of those your request becomes — that is exactly the state machine a status edit would push onto you, and getting it wrong would leave a child enrolled.

Ending an enrollment that has already ended returns `200` with the existing record, so a retry you could not confirm reaches the same place rather than a conflict you must interpret.

end_date.description: Optional. Supply it to schedule the ending; omit it to close an enrollment whose end date has passed.

post.summary: Void an enrollment that never represented service
post.description:
Records that an enrollment was created or activated in error and never represented service. Requires the `enrollment.write` scope.

**Three endings, and they are not interchangeable.** `ended` says service happened and concluded. `canceled` says a commitment was withdrawn before it began. `voided` says the record was never real at all. `POST /enrollments/end` reaches the first two; only this reaches the third. Ending a mistaken enrollment would assert that care was delivered, and would keep the child on your roster as genuine history.

**It is refused where it would be a lie.** If attendance was recorded under the enrollment then a child actually arrived, and no operator decision changes that. Alloy checks its own attendance ledger — reversed and superseded facts do not count — and returns `409` if any effective fact remains. Use `POST /enrollments/end` for history you regret; this is for records that were never true. A `canceled` enrollment is also refused: it already tells a narrower true story.

**What it does to the rest.** The child stops being visible through this enrollment: they leave `GET /api/v1/children`, their household leaves `GET /api/v1/households` and their edges leave `GET /api/v1/relationships`, exactly as a cancellation does. Any placement or schedule assignment still attached is canceled in the same act, so nothing operational is left pointing at an enrollment that says it was never valid.

**Nothing disappears.** The enrollment stays readable on `GET /api/v1/enrollments` with `status: "voided"`, and its update clock advances, so the transition reaches you on a normal `updated_since` or `since_token` pass. Treat a child leaving `/children` as a signal to read `/enrollments`.

**Safe to retry.** Voiding an already-voided enrollment returns it unchanged with `200`.

**This supersedes rather than edits.** Alloy writes a new placement naming the one it replaces and closes the prior one the day before the move. A copy you already synchronized is therefore never silently wrong — you receive the change through ordinary incremental synchronization, and the placement that applied last month still reads as it did.

Changes a child's committed schedule from a date. Requires the `schedule.write` scope.

**This is a named operation, not a field edit.** The public API has no `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` on any resource. Alloy performs the intent through the same authority its own surfaces use, so its validation and refusals are what you receive.

**This supersedes rather than edits**, exactly as placement does: a new assignment naming the one it replaces, with the prior one closed the day before.

It never touches a generated schedule day. A day is a view of the commitment — changing a day means changing the assignment it came from, which is this operation.

post.summary: Cancel a placement that was never effective
post.description:
Cancels a placement that should never have existed. Requires the `enrollment.write` scope.

**This is not ``/placements/move``, and the difference is the point.** Moving says the earlier record was true and then stopped being true: Alloy closes it on the day before the replacement begins, so it keeps asserting the period it covered. Cancelling says it was NEVER effective — recorded against the wrong child, or with terms nobody ever agreed. Using `/placements/move` for a mistake would publish a period of service that never happened, and you would have no way to tell the two apart afterwards.

**Nothing is deleted.** The record is retained and its `status` becomes `canceled`, so an identifier you already synchronised still resolves and explains itself. Poll `status` to converge: `canceled` means it never took effect and nothing should be derived from it.

**Safe to retry.** Cancelling an already-canceled record returns it unchanged with `200` rather than a conflict, so an attempt you could not confirm reaches the same place.

Only a record that is still operational can be canceled. One that has already ended or been superseded asserts that service really happened, and denying it retroactively would break every figure derived from it; that returns `409`.

post.description:
Cancels a schedule assignment that should never have applied. Requires the `schedule.write` scope.

**This is not ``/schedule-assignments/change``, and the difference is the point.** Changing says the earlier record was true and then stopped being true: Alloy closes it on the day before the replacement begins, so it keeps asserting the period it covered. Cancelling says it was NEVER effective — recorded against the wrong child, or with terms nobody ever agreed. Using `/schedule-assignments/change` for a mistake would publish a period of service that never happened, and you would have no way to tell the two apart afterwards.

**Nothing is deleted.** The record is retained and its `status` becomes `canceled`, so an identifier you already synchronised still resolves and explains itself. Poll `status` to converge: `canceled` means it never took effect and nothing should be derived from it.

**Safe to retry.** Cancelling an already-canceled record returns it unchanged with `200` rather than a conflict, so an attempt you could not confirm reaches the same place.

Only a record that is still operational can be canceled. One that has already ended or been superseded asserts that service really happened, and denying it retroactively would break every figure derived from it; that returns `409`.

**It also stops the derived days.** `GET /api/v1/schedule-days` expands assignments into concrete expected days; a canceled assignment stops projecting, so you will not keep receiving attendance expectations nobody ever owed.

bearerAuth.description: An opaque access token from /api/v1/oauth/token. Not a JWT; do not parse it.

RequestId.description: Server-generated identifier for this request. Quote it to support. Present on every response.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests permitted in the current window.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests remaining in the current window.

client_secret.description: Shown once at creation and never retrievable afterwards.

scope.description: Space-delimited scopes the installation currently grants. Informational — authority is re-read from the installation on every request, not carried by the token.

location_ids.description: An EMPTY list denies everything. It never means all locations.

code.description: Stable and machine-readable. Branch on this.

message.description: For humans. NOT a contract; it may change.

Location.description: A canonical Alloy location. `id` is Alloy's canonical identity; correlate your own identifiers separately rather than expecting Alloy to carry them.

id.description: Canonical Alloy identifier. Opaque — do not parse.

unit_role.description: Topology role, units only. Null means unknown — it was never back-filled to a guess.

site_id.description: The site this location sits under, resolved by Alloy's site-resolution authority. Null for an orphan.

updated_at.description: Resync watermark. Re-request from slightly BEFORE your last value and upsert — it is wall-clock and not transactionally ordered.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor`. Null means the last page — you never need a request to discover there is nothing left.

sync_token.description: Exact position of the last record on this page. Persist it after a successful pass and pass it back as `since_token` to resume. Returned on every page that has records, including the last one.

AttendanceEvent.description: One canonical attendance fact. Append-only: a mistake is corrected by a later event that names this one, never by changing it.

id.description: Stable identifier for this attendance fact.

child_id.description: The Alloy identifier of the child this fact is about.

child_external_id.description: Your own identifier for this child, as your installation has mapped it. Null when you have not mapped one. It is the identifier you supplied for the child, returned so you can match this fact to your own record without keeping a second lookup table.

site_id.description: The site the fact was recorded at. Always within your installation's location boundary.

room_id.description: The room the fact happened in, for facts that name one. A room is a location of type `unit`; the same identifier appears in GET /api/v1/locations.

from_room_id.description: The room a child moved out of. Present only on a `room_transfer`.

to_room_id.description: The room a child moved into. Present only on a `room_transfer`.

event_kind.description: What happened: `check_in` and `check_out` are arrival and departure, `room_transfer` is a move between rooms, `absence` records an expected child who did not attend, `present` is an observed presence without a recorded arrival, and `schedule_override` records an operational change to the day itself.

entry_type.description: Whether this fact stands alone or acts on an earlier one. `original` is a first statement. `correction` restates a fact that was wrong, and the restated values are on the correction. `reversal` voids a fact that should not have been recorded and asserts nothing in its place. Both name their target in `corrects_event_id`.

corrects_event_id.description: The attendance fact this one supersedes, for corrections and reversals.

service_date.description: The operating day this fact belongs to, in the organization's configured operational timezone. It is determined when the fact is recorded and is never recomputed afterwards. It is NOT the UTC date of `event_at`: a late-evening arrival and an early-morning one can share an operating day while falling on different UTC dates, and the reverse.

actor_type.description: The kind of actor the fact was recorded by — a staff member, a parent, a guardian, an emergency contact, or an automated system. Alloy never identifies the individual here.

source.description: The channel the fact was captured through. `integration_api` means it arrived through this API; `kiosk`, `staff_workspace`, `parent_portal` and `door_access` are the operational channels Alloy itself records through. Useful for telling your own writes apart from everyone else's.

recorded_at.description: When Alloy recorded it. This is the field incremental synchronization advances on, and the order the collection returns.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when this is the last page.

sync_token.description: Exact position of the last record on this page. Persist it after a successful pass and pass it back as `since_token` to resume. Returned on every page that has records, including the last one.

AttendanceSubmissionEvent.description: One attendance fact you are asserting. Corrections and reversals are submitted the same way, naming the event they supersede.

external_event_id.description: YOUR stable identifier for this event. It is the replay identity: submitting the same id again returns the fact already recorded rather than creating a second one. Unique within your installation.

event_kind.description: What happened. `check_in` and `room_transfer` require the relevant room identifiers.

child_external_id.description: Your identifier for the child, as mapped for this installation. Alloy never creates a child from an identifier it does not know.

room_external_id.description: Your identifier for the room. Required for `check_in`.

from_room_external_id.description: Your identifier for the room being left. Used with `room_transfer`.

to_room_external_id.description: Your identifier for the room being entered. Used with `room_transfer`.

occurred_at.description: When it physically happened. Must carry a timezone offset or Z.

recorded_at.description: When your system recorded it, if that differs from when it happened.

corrects_external_event_id.description: The `external_event_id` of an event you previously submitted and Alloy accepted. Required for a correction or reversal.

correction_mode.description: `correction` restates the earlier fact with the values on this event. `reversal` voids it and asserts nothing in its place. Defaults to `correction` when `corrects_external_event_id` is present.

AttendanceSubmissionResult.description: What happened to one submitted event. Every event you send gets exactly one of these.

external_event_id.description: The identifier you supplied, so results can be matched to your batch in any order.

outcome.description: `accepted` — a canonical fact was recorded. `replayed` — you had already sent this event; the fact that exists is returned and nothing was created. `pending_mapping` — the event is stored but an identifier is not yet mapped, so it could not be attributed; submit it again once the mapping exists. `conflict` — this id was already accepted carrying different content. `rejected` — Alloy will not record this event; `code` says why.

attendance_event_id.description: The canonical fact, for `accepted` and `replayed`. Readable immediately through GET /api/v1/attendance-events.

code.description: Stable machine-readable reason. Null when accepted or replayed.

message.description: One sentence describing what to do about it.

events.description: Up to 200 events. Each is judged on its own.

Child.description: A child with an enrollment that represented service — neither canceled before it began nor voided as recorded in error. Identity and lifecycle only — health, allergy and safeguarding information is never part of this resource.

external_id.description: Your own identifier for this child, if you have mapped one. Only your installation's mapping is ever returned.

household_id.description: The household this child belongs to. Read it with `GET /api/v1/households`.

status.description: Poll this to learn when a child leaves service. A child is never removed from history without this changing first.

status_key.description: The operator-facing lifecycle label, when one is set.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

sync_token.description: Checkpoint of the last row on this page. Store it and pass it back as `since_token` to resume exactly here.

Household.description: The household a visible child belongs to. A thin anchor for grouping siblings — never a grant of access to them.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

sync_token.description: Checkpoint of the last row on this page. Store it and pass it back as `since_token` to resume exactly here.

Relationship.description: One adult's relationship to one child. Relationships are edges with their own identity, because the same person can hold different authority for different children.

person_id.description: Alloy's identifier for the adult. Stable across every relationship they hold.

email.description: Present only when the installation holds `relationships.contact.read`. The field is absent entirely without it.

phone.description: Present only when the installation holds `relationships.contact.read`.

priority.description: Contact order, lowest first, when the operator has set one.

pickup_authorized.description: Whether this person may collect this child RIGHT NOW. This is an effective answer computed by Alloy, not a stored flag: it is true only when collection authority has been granted, nothing currently withdraws it, and the child is inside your boundary. It fails closed — anything uncertain is false. No reason is ever returned, and you should not infer one.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

sync_token.description: Checkpoint of the last row on this page. Store it and pass it back as `since_token` to resume exactly here.

Enrollment.description: A committed enrollment agreement: this child is enrolled at this site, from this date. It is not the room (see Placements) and not the days (see Schedule assignments).

end_date.description: Null while the agreement is open. Poll for this to learn that enrollment has ended.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

sync_token.description: Checkpoint of the last row on this page. Store it and pass it back as `since_token` to resume exactly here.

Placement.description: Committed room placement, effective-dated. Corrections arrive as a NEW placement naming the one it replaces, so a stored copy is never silently wrong.

room_location_id.description: A Location id of type `unit` from `GET /api/v1/locations`.

supersedes_placement_id.description: The placement this one replaces, when it is a correction.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

sync_token.description: Checkpoint of the last row on this page. Store it and pass it back as `since_token` to resume exactly here.

ScheduleAssignment.description: The committed, effective-dated schedule commitment for a child — standing intent, not individual days. Only children appear here.

pattern_label.description: The operator's name for the recurring pattern, such as a full-week or part-week schedule.

weekdays.description: Days the pattern recurs on, 0 = Sunday.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

sync_token.description: Checkpoint of the last row on this page. Store it and pass it back as `since_token` to resume exactly here.

ScheduleDay.description: One expected day for one child, generated from a committed schedule assignment. Not a stored record — it has no identifier of its own and no change history.

schedule_assignment_id.description: The committed assignment this day was derived from. Synchronize that resource to be told when it changes.

ScheduleDayWindow.description: A derived window. Deliberately carries no cursor and no sync token.

derived_from.description: Names the canonical authority these rows were computed from.

Staff.description: A person employed by the organization, composed with their employment. Alloy has no separate staff record: `id` is the employment, `person_id` is the human.

id.description: The employment identifier. Use it as the stable key for this staff member's engagement.

email.description: Present only when the installation holds `staff.contact.read`.

phone.description: Present only when the installation holds `staff.contact.read`.

position_label.description: The job title as the operator names it.

primary_location_id.description: A Location id from `GET /api/v1/locations`. Staff are visible only when this is inside your boundary.

sync_token.description: Checkpoint of the last row on this page. Store it and pass it back as `since_token` to resume exactly here.

EnrollmentOperationResult.description: The enrollment as it now stands.

PlacementOperationResult.description: The placement as it now stands.

supersedes_placement_id.description: The placement this one replaces, when it is a move.

InvalidRequest.description: The request contains an invalid or unsupported parameter, filter, cursor, sync token, or date value.

InvalidCredential.description: Authentication failed. Present valid credentials or obtain a new access token, then retry.
